$comment: AITP Ed25519 and P-256 keypair known-answer test vectors. Pinned reference values for cross-implementation interop. RFC-AITP-0001 §5.3 references this file. Each entry takes a 32-byte seed and pins the resulting raw Ed25519 public key (base64url, unpadded, 43 chars) and the corresponding aid:pubkey: identifier.

vectors.$comment: Added to support 3-hop multi-hop delegation fixtures (RFC-AITP-0011). Standard deterministic seed pattern (0x01 repeated 32 times); a 4-byte distinct-from-the-other-three seed is sufficient for cross-impl interop, since the AID derivation is fixed by Ed25519.

First non-Ed25519 reference keypair. Added in v0.2 to support cross-impl conformance for RFC-AITP-0001 §5.4.3 algorithm-tagged signatures. Algorithm: ECDSA on P-256 with SHA-256. Private scalar is the 32-byte big-endian integer 0x05*32 (mod n); public key is the SEC1 compressed point form (33 bytes). The aid grammar uses the v0.2 algorithm-tagged form `aid:pubkey:p256:<44-char-base64url>`.

UNTRUSTED non-role key. Exists solely so mh-002 (RFC-AITP-0004 §5, MANIFEST_SIGNATURE_INVALID) is independently re-mintable: an implementer needs the ATTACKER's private key to produce a valid proof_of_possession.signature before the Manifest signature check is even reached (RFC-AITP-0003 §5 verifies PoP before signature). This key is deliberately NOT one of the agentA-D role keys above and MUST NOT be added to any trust_anchors / pinned_keys fixture — its only legitimate use is minting the attacker-signed content of mh-002. Seed pattern 0xAA × 32, chosen to be distinct from every other seed in this file (0x00, 0x00..1f, 0xff, 0x01, 0x05 repeats). Replaces mh-002's original attacker AID, whose seed was never published and is unrecoverable (issue #17 erratum 2); mh-002's signatures were placeholders, so nothing pinned depended on the old AID.

The same keypair as kat-keypair-001 (seed = 32 zero bytes), written in the v0.2 algorithm-tagged AID form `aid:pubkey:ed25519:<43-char-base64url>` (RFC-AITP-0001 §5.3). Every other Ed25519 entry in this file uses the untagged form, which `untagged_aid` repeats here. The two strings name the same key, but they are different byte strings wherever an AID enters a signing input (for example the RFC-AITP-0002 §3.1 proof_input), so an implementation MUST carry the AID string it was given rather than re-deriving one form from the key.
